# netcup_clouddns_record (Resource)

Manages one netcup CloudDNS record using strict, automatically committed changesets. Other records are preserved. Requires clouddns_api_key; legacy CCP DNS credentials cannot be used. Import with domain_id/record_identifier. Do not manage the same record through multiple resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Supply NETCUP_CLOUDDNS_API_KEY from your secret manager.
data "netcup_clouddns_domains" "all" {}

resource "netcup_clouddns_record" "www" {
  domain_id = one([
    for domain in data.netcup_clouddns_domains.all.domains : domain.id
    if domain.fqdn == "example.com" && domain.is_dns_managed
  ])
  name  = "www"
  type  = "A"
  rdata = "192.0.2.10"
  ttl   = 300
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (Number) Domain ID from netcup_clouddns_domains.
- `name` (String) Record name relative to the zone; use @ for the apex or * for a wildcard.
- `rdata` (String) Record data in zone-file presentation format. For MX use priority hostname, for SRV priority weight port target. TXT quoting follows the netcup API.
- `ttl` (Number) Record TTL in seconds, at least 1.
- `type` (String) Uppercase DNS record type.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite domain_id/record_identifier. Record identifiers can change when a revision replaces a record.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Use the domain ID and a record identifier from netcup_clouddns_records.
terraform import netcup_clouddns_record.www '12345/59994952-e024-4871-b04d-546d66f25e73'
```
